newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian liberalisation seen surviving Congress woes.
newsitem.headline: Indian liberalisation seen surviving Congress woes.

text.p: Turmoil in India's oldest political party will not affect the liberal economic policies pursued by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition, analysts said on Monday.

Former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, who launched the liberalisation drive in 1991, quit as Congress party chief on Saturday after a court upheld a summons ordering him to appear in a $100,000 criminal conspiracy case.
The Congress leadership was to meet on Monday evening to elect an interim chief.
Deve Gowda's minority government depends on support from Congress, which has 140 lawmakers in the 545-member parliament, to survive.
"These changes will have no effect on the liberalisation process," V. Raghuraman, secretary general of Associated Chambers of Commerce (Assocham), told Reuters.
Deve Gowda has to walk a tightrope between coalition partners ranging from free-market centrists to communists, while keeping an eye on Congress.
But this has not deterred him from pressing ahead with the reforms launched by Rao by taking steps to open up the economy.

"The investment climate in the country has become more conducive and the government's involvement has (been) reduced considerably due to delicensing and deregulation. We are committed to continue in this direction," Deve Gowda recently told a business conference.
Analysts said the changes in Congress leadership would have little impact on economic decision-making.
Raghuraman said the liberal group within the ruling coalition has been able to push reforms forward, and predicted the process would not be halted.
"I do not think it will have any impact on government policies," said an analyst with a foreign securities firm who asked not to be identified.
